item.title: Miho no Matsubara: The Legendary Pine Grove With Mount Fuji Views — Guide
item.description: Miho no Matsubara is a seven-kilometre stretch of coastline planted with some 30,000 pine trees, framing one of Japan’s most celebrated views: Mount Fuji rising across the waters of Suruga Bay beyond the black-sand beach and twisted pines. The grove is a component site of Mount Fuji’s UNESCO World Heritage listing and the setting of the famous Hagoromo legend, in which a celestial maiden left her feathered robe hanging on a pine here, a story still honoured at the ‘Hagoromo pine’ and in Noh theatre.

item.title: Chureito Pagoda: The Iconic Five-Storey Pagoda With Mount Fuji — Guide
item.description: Chureito Pagoda is a five-storey red pagoda set on a hillside above Fujiyoshida, reached by a climb of just under 400 steps, and frames one of Japan’s most iconic views: the vermilion pagoda in the foreground with Mount Fuji rising behind it across the town below. The scene is especially striking in spring when cherry blossoms surround the pagoda, and in autumn with coloured foliage, drawing photographers from around the world to what has become one of the most recognisable images of Japan.

item.title: Fuji-Q Highland: Record-Breaking Roller Coasters Beneath Mount Fuji — Guide
item.description: Fuji-Q Highland is a major amusement park at the foot of Mount Fuji, famous for its collection of record-breaking roller coasters, several of which have held world records for height, speed or number of inversions, all set against the dramatic backdrop of the mountain itself. Beyond the thrill rides, the park offers themed attractions, character-based areas popular with families, and a notoriously long and elaborate haunted-house attraction, making it a popular day out combining adrenaline with unbeatable Fuji views.

item.title: Kawaguchiko Lakeside Cycling: Circle the Lake Beneath Mount Fuji — Guide
item.description: Cycling around Lake Kawaguchiko is one of the most enjoyable ways to experience the Fuji Five Lakes, following a mostly flat route that circles the lake with ever-changing views of Mount Fuji reflected across the water. Rental shops near Kawaguchiko Station offer bicycles, including e-bikes for the gentle hills, and the roughly 18-kilometre loop passes quiet lakeside stretches, viewpoints, cafes, museums and hot springs, letting riders set their own pace and stop wherever the Fuji views are best.

item.title: Lake Yamanakako SUP: Paddleboarding Beneath Mount Fuji — Guide
item.description: Lake Yamanakako is the largest and highest of the Fuji Five Lakes, and its relatively calm, shallow waters make it a popular spot for stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) with an unbeatable backdrop: Mount Fuji rising directly across the lake. Rental operators and guided sessions cater to beginners and experienced paddlers alike, and gliding across the water with the mountain reflected below is one of the region’s most memorable and photogenic water experiences, especially in the calm conditions of early morning.
